name: H. C. Pollitt
bio: Herbert Charles Pollitt, a native of Kendal in Westmorland and an undergraduate at Trinity College, Cambridge, 1889-92, where he made a name as an amateur ballet dancer. He collected Beardsley drawings, which he bought from Wilde's publisher Leonard Smithers. He preferred 'Jerome' to his own Christian names and signed himself so in his letters to Wilde; his Kendal home was called The Green Window. Wilde corresponded with him between November 1898 and January 1899 and appears never to have met him - in January 1899 he was still asking Smithers what Pollitt was like. Wilde sent him inscribed copies of the French translation of The Ballad of Reading Gaol and of The Importance of Being Earnest, and, per the editors, misspelt his surname in all four of the surviving letters.
bio_note: All facts from Holland & Hart-Davis, Complete Letters (2000) with printed folios confirmed. Birth and death years, Kendal, Trinity College 1889-92, the amateur ballet dancing, the Beardsley collecting bought from Smithers, the preference for 'Jerome' and the inscribed presentation copies are from the main-particulars footnote at p. 1103 n. 1 (PDF 1149). 'Pollitt's Kendal home was called The Green Window' is p. 1107 n. 1 (PDF 1153). The four surviving letters and the misspelling in all of them are p. 1120 n. 2 (PDF 1166); the misspelt envelope address itself is quoted at p. 1116 n. 1 (PDF 1162). The never-met reading rests on Wilde's own question to Smithers at p. 1117 (PDF 1163). Nothing read so far states how or when Wilde and Pollitt were introduced to each other by correspondence; the earlier index locator at printed 1103 is the first letter, and no Pollitt letter to Wilde is printed in this edition.
